data.one_liner: Simplifies and speeds up creation of in-memory and persistent caching mechanisms using code generation.
data.what_it_does: The package generates caching code for Dart classes and methods. It supports LRU eviction, time-to-live (TTL), conditional caching, persistent storage integration, and stream updates.
use_when: You want to automatically cache API responses or expensive method calls in memory or persistent storage.
You need LRU cache eviction or TTL-based expiration without writing manual cache boilerplate.
avoid_when: You do not want to use code generation or build_runner in your project.
You need a general-purpose key-value store without class-level annotations.
strengths: Reduces boilerplate for caching method results.
Supports LRU cache algorithm, TTL, and conditional caching via 'where'.
Supports persistent storage integrations and cache streams.
weaknesses: Requires running build_runner for code generation.
Deprecated persistentStorage parameter requires migrating to newer annotations.
data.setup_notes: Add cached and build_runner to dev_dependencies, add cached_annotation to dependencies, and run build_runner.

alternatives.name: flutter_cache_manager
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need to cache web files, images, or downloads instead of arbitrary method results.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you just need simple key-value persistence without method-level caching annotations.
